headline: US stocks ended mixed as hawkish Fed minutes and Nvidia’s post-earnings slide weighed on sentiment while healthcare slumped on Medicare audit fears and AI IPO enthusiasm built ahead of Anthropic’s debut
raw_text:
- The S&P 500 ($SPX) fell 0.23% to 7,323.63 for a fifth straight loss and the Dow Jones Industrial Average ($DJI) dropped 1.11% (561 points) to 50,198.17, while the Nasdaq Composite ($COMP) rose 0.42% to 24,429.88 and the Russell 2000 (IWM) gained 0.46% to 2,714.31.
- Healthcare stocks slumped on Medicare Advantage audit scrutiny and a proposed audit rule from the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, with UnitedHealth Group (UNH) down 10.21%, Humana (HUM) off 12.98%, Elevance (ELV) lower by 7.6%, and Centene (CNC) by 7.1%, dragging the Dow.
- Nvidia (NVDA) reported Q3 revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% year-over-year and above estimates, guided to roughly $130 billion in Q4 revenue and 75% growth in fiscal 2028, but its shares fell 2.9% to $150.96 after Moody’s cut its credit outlook to stable, citing leadership uncertainty following Jensen Huang’s ouster, halted China AI chip shipments, and regulatory risks.
- Consumer discretionary led the market as TJX Companies (TJX) jumped 8.05% after missing EPS estimates but raising full-year guidance, while Target (TGT) gained about 4% on an earnings beat and higher guidance and Take-Two Interactive (TTWO) climbed more than 6% on strong GTA 6 pre-orders and reviews.
- Technology also outperformed, with AMD (AMD) up 5.3% and Broadcom (AVGO) gaining 3.7%, making consumer discretionary and tech two of the six S&P 500 sectors that finished higher, while energy weakened alongside lower oil (@CL) prices.
- Cybersecurity names rallied broadly on Nvidia (NVDA)’s upbeat results and technology-outage concerns, with Palo Alto Networks (PANW) advancing nearly 10%, CrowdStrike (CRWD) rising about 8%, and Fortinet (FTNT) up 6%.
- In after-hours trading, Palo Alto Networks (PANW) climbed further after beating earnings and announcing a $4.5 billion acquisition, while CrowdStrike (CRWD) and Okta (OKTA) also rose, and BellRing Brands (BRBR) surged 24% following its report.
- Fed minutes showed officials expected additional rate hikes and flagged concerns that artificial intelligence could sustain inflation, with Governor Christopher Waller even highlighting the possibility of a 50 basis point “shock” move.
- Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 per share, above the prior $70–$78 target range, implying a roughly $1.5 trillion valuation ahead of Thursday’s debut under ticker ANT (ANT).
- Traders are positioning for tomorrow’s catalysts including Walmart (WMT) earnings, Anthropic’s IPO listing under ticker ANT (ANT), and further commentary from Federal Reserve officials.
